items.axis: observability honesty / token efficiency / protocol reliability
items.title: Make startup-brief freshness session-aware so a new agent never inherits stale context-meter or doctor evidence as live truth.
items.why: scripts/check-brief-staleness.mjs accepts any coherent same-date brief for 48 hours. This session declared fresh while the brief still showed the prior 200k unknown/default context meter and old doctor tally, contradicting the live 1M Codex meter and doctor receipt.
items.recipe: Parse the active session lock and brief generation/session metadata; mark a brief stale when the lock is newer or its agent/session evidence cannot match; add fail-closed unit tests and regenerate through the existing renderer.

L1.recipe: Treat any active lock newer than the brief file as stale.

L2.recipe: Extract a testable freshness evaluator covering coherent, aged and new-lock cases.

L3.recipe: Add session-aware freshness with reason codes, JSON evidence, regression tests and a newly rendered canonical brief.

items.axis: competitive trust / input reliability / feedback loop
items.title: Make explicit and background-tab pauses observable, input-safe replay transitions instead of invisible simulation freezes.
items.why: The replay analyzer and edge validator count pause as an interaction, but App.jsx never records pause. The live loop has no visibilitychange contract, so hidden-tab throttling can freeze a competitive run without a trace transition or guaranteed held-input release.
items.recipe: Add a pure pause-transition planner plus one App pause coordinator; auto-pause on hidden visibility, release held fire/touch/gamepad input, record bounded pause/resume commands, expose an honest auto-pause reason in PauseMenu, and test explicit, visibility and idempotent transitions.

L1.recipe: Record explicit pause and resume commands.

L2.recipe: Centralize pause toggles and auto-pause on page hide while releasing held input.

L3.recipe: Ship the tested visibility-aware transition contract, accessible reason copy and replay-evidence assertions without changing score eligibility claims.

items.title: Fail protocol drift when a local skill points at a missing canonical section or helper.
items.why: The audit skill points to docs/SESSION_PROTOCOL.md section 2B and its Oracle helper, but this repo has neither. npm run protocol:drift still reports Status: ok because it checks file presence, not referenced section or helper reachability.
items.recipe: Restore the public-safe local section 2B audit protocol, route Oracle through the existing Studio Ops proxy instead of a missing local binary, and extend protocol-drift tests to verify section anchors and executable helper routes.

L2.recipe: Check all four arc phase section anchors and a local Oracle route.

L3.recipe: Ship anchor-aware protocol drift, the missing audit section, a Windows-hidden Oracle proxy and regression coverage.

items.title: Convert adaptive reduced-effects behavior into a bounded, local run-performance receipt with an actionable recommendation.
items.why: useGameLoop counts slow frames and flips window.__codReducedEffects, but resets evidence every 120 frames. DeathScreen cannot distinguish adaptive protection from an ordinary run, and no bounded p95/drop receipt survives for device QA.
items.recipe: Extract a pure bounded frame monitor with hysteresis, percentiles and snapshots; keep hot-path memory constant; attach its local-only receipt to run history and death props; show a concise PERFORMANCE ASSISTED card only when sustained drops occurred; never invalidate or overclaim competitive causality.

L1.recipe: Expose total, slow and worst frame counters from makeFrameMonitor.

L2.recipe: Add bounded histogram percentiles, hysteresis and a snapshot callback.

L3.recipe: Persist one sanitized local run receipt, render an accessible recommendation at death and test boundedness, hysteresis and honesty language.

items.axis: feature depth / progression economy / runtime organization
items.title: Route railgun and projectile enemy defeats through one deterministic economy plan so weapon choice cannot drift reward semantics.
items.why: App.jsx contains separate large railgun and projectile defeat blocks with duplicated boss classification, combo, score and coin-drop formulas. The formulas already differ in surrounding side effects, making future progression changes path-dependent and hard to verify.
items.recipe: Extract a pure enemy-defeat economy planner for score, boss identity and named-RNG coin drops; feed both railgun and projectile paths through it; preserve exact current outputs with seeded fixtures; document the remaining orchestration boundary in the App extraction roadmap.

L2.recipe: Share score, boss and coin plan data with deterministic tests.

L3.recipe: Ship one pure defeat-economy contract across both weapon paths with seeded parity fixtures and extraction-roadmap evidence.
